title: Encapsulation: why an accessor is not red tape

videos.script: Lesson 14 made private the sensible default. This lesson says what it buys you. {{open}} It starts with a book whose year is a public field. Anybody can set it to minus eighteen ninety-nine, and the program prints it without a murmur. {{private}} Then the same book with the field private, a getter, and a setter that checks. The bad year now stops the program, on the line that wrote it. {{leak}} Next, a shelf for two books that ends up holding three. Its list was private. Its getter handed the list out anyway. {{copy}} Two ways to hand out a list safely, a copy and a read-only view, and how they differ. {{tell}} Last, a rule about where code belongs. Instead of asking a loan for its dates and working out the fee yourself, you ask the loan for the fee. By the end you can tell an accessor that protects something from one that is only ceremony.
